# US return and refund rules

If you sell to customers in the United States, then federal and state rules affect how you handle returns and refunds. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule requires that you ship orders within the time stated in your ad or, if no time is stated, within 30 days.

When you can't ship on time, you must notify the customer and offer the option to cancel the order for a full refund. Refunds for cancelled orders must be issued within seven working days for card payments. The FTC does not require you to accept returns of delivered goods, but if you post a return policy you must honor it.

Some states, such as California and New York, require that you display your return and refund policy conspicuously at the point of sale. If no policy is displayed, customers in those states may return goods for a full refund within a statutory period. These rules apply only to sales to customers located in the United States; they do not cover the withdrawal rights of consumers in the European Union.
